102514.m: Bertrand Piccard comes from a family of scientists.

102515.q: In which Swiss city did Daniel Bernoulli live and teach?
102515.e: Daniel Bernoulli came from a Basel family and was a professor at the University of Basel for a long time.

102516.q: What did Daniel Bernoulli study in particular?
102516.e: Bernoulli studied how liquids and gases flow. His findings help today with building pipes and aeroplanes.
102516.m: Bernoulli studied flowing water and flowing air.

102517.q: What does Daniel Bernoulli's law describe?
102517.e: Bernoulli found out that where air or water flows fast, the pressure is lower. This helps, for example, to understand how aeroplanes fly.
102517.m: According to Bernoulli, fast-flowing air pushes less.

102518.q: Which subject did Daniel Bernoulli study besides mathematics?
102518.e: Daniel Bernoulli first studied medicine and became a doctor. Alongside that he learnt a lot of mathematics from his father.

102519.q: What was Daniel Bernoulli's father's job?
102519.e: His father Johann Bernoulli was a famous mathematician in Basel. There were many scientists in the family.
102519.m: Daniel Bernoulli's father was a mathematician.

102520.q: The Basel scientist Daniel Bernoulli lived from 1700 to 1782. Which century was that?
102520.e: The years from 1701 to 1800 make up the 18th century. Bernoulli lived almost entirely in this period.
102520.m: Daniel Bernoulli lived in the 18th century.

102521.q: In which century did Daniel Bernoulli live?
102521.e: Daniel Bernoulli was born in 1700 and died in Basel in 1782. So he lived in the 18th century.
102521.m: Daniel Bernoulli lived in the 18th century.

102522.q: You blow between two sheets of paper hanging down. What happens?
a: They spin round in a circle
102522.e: Where the air flows fast, it pushes less. The still air outside pushes the sheets together.

102523.q: Which word is Archimedes said to have shouted after a discovery?
102523.e: “Eureka” is Greek and means “I have found it”. That is how Archimedes is said to have shown his joy.

102524.q: According to a story, where did Archimedes have his famous idea?
102524.e: Archimedes got into a full bath, and water overflowed. Then he understood how to measure the volume of things.
102524.m: Archimedes had his idea in the bath.

102525.q: According to Archimedes, which simple tool can you use to lift heavy things?
102525.e: Archimedes explained the law of the lever. With a long bar and a fixed pivot you can lift heavy loads.
102525.m: With a lever you can lift heavy things more easily.

102526.q: What was Archimedes asked to check for the king?
a: Whether a crown was pure gold
102526.e: The king wanted to know whether the goldsmith had cheated him. Archimedes tested the crown with water.
102526.m: Archimedes tested the king's golden crown.

102527.q: What did Archimedes explain about things in water?
102527.e: Archimedes discovered buoyancy. Water pushes things upwards, which is why ships float, for example.

102528.q: Which country did Michael Faraday come from?
102528.e: Michael Faraday was born in 1791 near London in England.

102529.q: Which trade did Michael Faraday learn as a teenager?
102529.e: Faraday did an apprenticeship as a bookbinder. While doing it he read many books about science and became curious.
102529.m: Faraday first trained as a bookbinder.

102530.q: Which physical unit is named after Michael Faraday?
102530.e: The unit farad measures how much electrical charge a component can store. It honours Michael Faraday.
102530.m: The farad is named after Faraday.

102531.q: According to Michael Faraday, what can you produce with a magnet and a coil of wire?
102531.e: If you move a magnet inside a coil of wire, electricity flows. Faraday discovered this in 1831.
102531.m: A magnet moving in a coil produces electricity.

102532.q: Which part of a bicycle works because of Faraday's discovery?
102532.e: In a dynamo a magnet turns inside a coil of wire. That makes electricity for the bike light.
102532.m: A bike dynamo makes electricity with a magnet.

102533.q: Who did Michael Faraday give exciting talks for at Christmas?
102533.e: Faraday started Christmas lectures for young people in London. This tradition still exists there today.
102533.m: Faraday gave Christmas lectures for children.

102534.q: Which object did Michael Faraday give famous talks about?
102534.e: Faraday used a simple candle to explain what happens when something burns. The talks became famous as a book.
102534.m: Faraday explained the physics of a candle.

102535.q: Which machine that turns using electricity was Michael Faraday one of the first to build?
102535.e: In 1821 Faraday showed how electricity and a magnet can make a wire turn in a circle. That was an early electric motor.
102535.m: Faraday built one of the first electric motors.

102536.q: How many national parks does Switzerland have?
102536.e: Switzerland has only one national park, the Swiss National Park in the Engadine. There nature is allowed to develop completely freely.
102536.m: Switzerland has a single national park.

102537.q: What are visitors not allowed to do in the Swiss National Park?
102537.e: In the national park you must stay on the marked paths. That way animals and plants are not disturbed.
102537.m: In the national park you always stay on the path.

102538.q: Can dogs come into the Swiss National Park?
102538.e: Dogs are banned from the national park, even on a lead. They could disturb or frighten the wild animals.
102538.m: Dogs stay out of the national park.

102539.q: Which animal with large, curved horns lives in the Swiss National Park?
102539.e: Lots of ibex live in the national park. The males have large, curved horns and climb skilfully on steep rocks. The chamois has only small horns.
102539.m: The ibex is a skilful climber in the national park.

102540.q: Which large bird of prey was reintroduced in the Swiss National Park?
102540.e: The bearded vulture had died out in the Alps. From 1991, young bearded vultures were released in the national park.
102540.m: The bearded vulture flies over the national park again.

102541.q: Can you put up a tent in the Swiss National Park?
102541.e: In the national park you may not camp or stay overnight, except in the Chamanna Cluozza hut or the hotel. That way the animals have peace at night.
102541.m: There is no camping in the national park.

a: An area where nature is protected
A car park at the edge of a forest
102542.e: In a nature reserve, animals and plants are specially protected. Special rules apply there.
102542.m: In a nature reserve, nature comes first.

102543.q: How should dogs be walked in many nature reserves?
102543.e: In many nature reserves dogs must stay on a lead. Otherwise they could chase birds and wild animals.
102543.m: In a nature reserve, the dog belongs on a lead.

102544.q: Why do you stay on the path in a nature reserve?
a: So that animals and plants are protected
So that your shoes stay clean
Because otherwise it is too warm
102544.e: Next to the path, birds nest and rare plants grow. If you stay on the path, you don't trample anything.
102544.m: Staying on the path protects animals and plants.

102545.q: Which Swiss landscape is often a nature reserve because it is wet and soft?
102545.e: Moors are wet landscapes with rare plants and animals. In Switzerland many moors are strictly protected.

102546.q: What do you do with your rubbish in a nature reserve?
a: You take it back with you
You throw it into the bushes
You leave it by the path
102546.e: Rubbish doesn't belong in nature. You pack it up and throw it into the right bin at home.
102546.m: What you bring with you, you also take back.

102547.q: What is the best way to behave so as not to disturb animals in a nature reserve?
102547.e: Many animals are frightened by noise and run away. If you are quiet, you can even watch them better.
102547.m: If you are quiet, you don't disturb the animals.

102548.q: What do you call an area on the shore where lots of reeds grow and water birds nest?
102548.e: Wetlands such as reedy shores are important for water birds and frogs. Many of them are nature reserves.
102548.m: Many water birds nest in the reeds on the shore.

102549.q: What does a sign at the entrance to a nature reserve often show?
102549.e: The sign says what you may and may not do in the area. For example: stay on the path and don't pick plants.
102549.m: Signs at the entrance show the rules of the reserve.

102550.e: Pro Natura is a Swiss organisation that works to protect nature. It looks after many nature reserves.
102550.m: Pro Natura works for nature in Switzerland.

102551.q: What was Pro Natura founded for in 1909?
102551.e: Pro Natura was founded in 1909 to raise money for the new national park. With this money the area could be leased.
102551.m: Pro Natura helped to found the national park.

102552.q: Which of these nature conservation organisations is the oldest?
102552.e: Pro Natura was founded in 1909. The other three organisations were only set up later.
102552.m: Pro Natura is older than WWF Switzerland, Greenpeace Switzerland and BirdLife Switzerland.

102553.q: What does Pro Natura choose every year?
102553.e: Every year Pro Natura chooses an animal of the year. This way many people get to know an animal and its habitat better.
102553.m: Every year Pro Natura presents an animal of the year.

102554.q: What can children do in Pro Natura youth groups?
102554.e: In the youth groups children go outdoors. They watch animals, build nest boxes and learn a lot about nature.
102554.m: In Pro Natura youth groups, children experience nature.

102555.q: In which forest in Valais does Pro Natura run a centre?
102555.e: The Pro Natura Aletsch Centre is near Riederalp. From there you can see the Aletsch Forest and the Great Aletsch Glacier.
102555.m: Pro Natura has a nature centre by the Aletsch Forest.

102556.q: What does Pro Natura do with many areas in Switzerland?
a: It protects and looks after them
It turns them into car parks
102556.e: Pro Natura looks after several hundred protected areas in Switzerland. There it takes care of meadows, ponds and forests.
102556.m: Pro Natura looks after many protected areas in Switzerland.

102557.q: In which country does the worldwide WWF have its headquarters?
102557.e: The WWF has its international headquarters in Gland in the canton of Vaud, on Lake Geneva.
102557.m: The WWF has its headquarters in Switzerland.

102558.q: What can children and teenagers go on with WWF Switzerland?
102558.e: WWF Switzerland offers camps and trips for children. There they experience nature up close.
102558.m: With WWF Switzerland, children can go on nature camps.

102559.q: What do the letters WWF stand for today?
102559.e: WWF stands for World Wide Fund for Nature. It is a worldwide fund for nature.
102559.m: The WWF is a worldwide fund for nature.

102560.q: In which WWF campaign do people all over the world switch off the lights for one hour?
102560.e: During Earth Hour, people, cities and companies switch off their lights for one hour once a year. The WWF uses it to draw attention to climate protection.
102560.m: During Earth Hour the lights stay off for one hour.

102561.e: Littering means carelessly throwing away or leaving rubbish lying around. It dirties streets, parks and nature.
102561.m: Leaving rubbish lying around is littering.

102562.q: Where does a used paper tissue belong when you are out for a walk?
102562.e: Even small bits of rubbish belong in a bin. If there isn't one, you take it home with you.
102562.m: Rubbish always belongs in a bin.

102563.q: Why are discarded cigarette ends bad for nature?
102563.e: Cigarette ends contain poisonous substances. These get into the water and harm animals and plants.
102563.m: Cigarette ends poison water and soil.

102564.q: What is the right thing to do with an empty PET bottle?
a: Put it in the PET collection
102564.e: PET bottles go in the PET collection, for example at the shop. New bottles can be made from them.
102564.m: Empty PET bottles belong in the PET collection.

102565.q: What can happen to a bird if plastic string is lying around in nature?
a: It gets tangled up in it
It gets full from eating it
102565.e: Animals can get tangled up in plastic or eat it. This can make them ill or kill them.
102565.m: Plastic rubbish is dangerous for animals.

102566.q: What can happen in many Swiss municipalities if you throw rubbish on the ground?
a: You have to pay a fine
102566.e: Many cantons and municipalities have fines for littering. This is meant to help reduce the amount of rubbish lying around.
102566.m: If you drop litter, you can get a fine.

102567.q: What do people do on a clean-up day?
102567.e: On a clean-up day, lots of people collect rubbish together in nature or in town. That way the surroundings become clean again.
102567.m: On clean-up day, people collect rubbish together.

102568.q: What do you call wild plants that you are not allowed to pick or dig up?
102568.e: Rare wild plants are protected. You may not pick, dig up or damage them.
102568.m: Leave protected plants standing in nature.

102569.q: What is the best thing to do with a rare flower you find beautiful?
102569.e: A photo is a lovely memory. The flower stays where it is, can make seeds, and other people can enjoy it too.
102569.m: Photograph beautiful flowers instead of picking them.

102570.q: Why shouldn't you pick rare flowers?
a: So that they can make seeds
Because they grow back straight away
102570.e: Picked flowers can no longer make seeds. So there will be fewer of them the next year.

102571.q: Which rare, protected flower has a yellow bloom that looks like a little rounded pouch?
102571.e: The lady's slipper is a rare orchid. Part of its flower is yellow and looks like a little shoe.
102571.m: The lady's slipper is a protected orchid.

102572.q: Who is happy when flowers are left standing in the meadow?
102572.e: Bees and butterflies collect nectar and pollen from the flowers. Picked flowers are food they miss out on.
102572.m: Flowers in the meadow are food for insects.

102573.q: Which protected mountain flower is blue and has a bell-shaped bloom?
102573.e: Gentian grows in the Alps and has bright blue flowers. Many kinds of gentian are protected.
102573.m: The blue gentian is a protected alpine flower.

102574.q: What are you not allowed to do with the roots of wild plants in nature?
102574.e: Digging plants up removes them completely from their habitat. With protected plants this is forbidden.

102575.q: How big should a fire in a fire pit be?
a: Small and easy to keep an eye on
102575.e: A small fire is easy to control. A big fire can throw sparks into the forest.
102575.m: A small fire is a safe fire.

102576.q: What must you do before leaving the fire pit?
102576.e: You put the fire out with water until there are no more embers. Otherwise a forest fire could start.
102576.m: Put a fire out completely before you leave.

102577.q: Which wood do you collect for a fire in the forest?
102577.e: You use dry, dead wood lying on the ground. Living trees and branches are left alone.
102577.m: Only collect dead wood for a fire.

102578.q: What applies if it hasn't rained for a long time and there is a fire ban?
a: You light the fire at night
You light the fire in the grass
102578.e: When it is dry, even a single spark can start a forest fire. So when there is a fire ban, you don't light any fire at all.
102578.m: During a fire ban, no fires at all.

102579.q: What must you not burn on a fire?
102579.e: Burning plastic makes poisonous smoke. That is why plastic belongs in the rubbish and not on the fire.
102579.m: Plastic never goes on the fire.

102580.q: What should you always have nearby when grilling over a fire, so you can put it out?
102580.e: You can put the fire out with water at the end. Water is also quickly at hand if sparks fly.
102580.m: Always keep water ready by a fire.

102581.q: What do people in Switzerland often eat when grilling at a fire pit?
102581.e: The cervelat is a popular sausage for grilling. You put it on a stick and hold it over the embers.
102581.m: The cervelat is a popular sausage for grilling in Switzerland.

102582.q: What is a wildlife quiet zone?
a: An area where wild animals are left in peace
102582.e: In a wildlife quiet zone, wild animals are meant to stay undisturbed. People may not go in, or only on certain paths.
102582.m: In a wildlife quiet zone, wild animals have peace.

102583.q: In which season are wildlife quiet zones especially important?
102583.e: In winter animals find little food and have to save their strength. When they flee, they use up a lot of energy.
102583.m: In winter wild animals need peace especially.

102584.q: Why is it bad when an animal flees from skiers in winter?
a: It uses up a lot of strength
102584.e: Running in snow takes a lot of strength. Because there is little food, the animal can become weak.
102584.m: Fleeing costs wild animals a lot of strength in winter.

102585.q: Where should snowshoers walk near wildlife quiet zones?
102585.e: Marked routes lead past the animals' resting places. That way chamois and black grouse are not disturbed.
102585.m: In winter, stay on marked routes.

102586.q: Which mountain animal is protected in a wildlife quiet zone?
102586.e: Chamois live in the Swiss mountains. In winter they need peace so that they have enough strength.
102586.m: Chamois find peace in wildlife quiet zones.

102587.q: Which bird digs itself a snow cave in winter and needs peace there?
102587.e: In winter the black grouse rests in a hollow in the snow. If it is startled, it loses valuable energy.
102587.m: The black grouse rests in a snow cave in winter.

102588.q: How can you recognise a wildlife quiet zone out in the countryside?
102588.e: Wildlife quiet zones are marked with signs. You can also find them on maps and on the internet.
102588.m: Signs show where a wildlife quiet zone begins.

a: A path with information boards about nature
A path in a shopping centre
102589.e: Along a nature trail there are boards with information about trees, animals and plants. That way you learn while you walk.
102589.m: On a nature trail you learn while you walk.

102590.q: What do you find on the boards of a nature trail?
102590.e: The boards explain which trees, animals or plants live nearby. Sometimes there are little puzzles too.
102590.m: The boards on a nature trail explain nature.

102591.q: What is the barefoot path on some nature trails for?
a: To feel the ground with your feet
102591.e: On a barefoot path you walk over sand, wood, moss or stones. That way you experience the ground with your feet.
102591.m: On the barefoot path you feel nature with your feet.

102592.q: What do you often learn about on a forest trail?
102592.e: On a forest trail the trees are often labelled. That way you learn about beech, oak and spruce, for example.
102592.m: On a forest trail you learn about trees.

102593.q: What can you do at a listening post on some nature trails?
102593.e: At a listening post you press a button or turn a handle. Then you hear, for example, the calls of birds from the area.
102593.m: At the listening post you learn birdsong.

102594.q: What is especially good about a nature trail for school classes?
102594.e: On a nature trail you see plants and animals right there. That way you learn with all your senses.
102594.m: On a nature trail you learn outdoors with all your senses.

102595.q: What does a beaver build in a stream to hold back the water?
102595.e: The beaver builds dams from branches, mud and stones. This creates a pond where it is safe.
102595.m: The beaver holds back the water with a dam.

102596.q: What does a beaver's tail look like?
102596.e: The beaver has a wide, flat tail shaped like a paddle. It helps with swimming and steering.
102596.m: The beaver has a wide, flat tail.

102597.e: The beaver is a herbivore. It eats bark, twigs, leaves and water plants.

102598.q: What colour are a beaver's gnawing teeth?
102598.e: The front of a beaver's teeth is orange. It contains iron, which makes the teeth very hard.
102598.m: The beaver has hard, orange gnawing teeth.

102599.q: Where is the entrance to a beaver lodge?
102599.e: The entrance to the beaver lodge is under water. That way enemies can't get in so easily.
102599.m: The entrance to the beaver lodge is under water.

102600.q: What had happened to the beaver in Switzerland about 200 years ago?
102600.e: The beaver was hunted for its fur and meat and disappeared from Switzerland in the 19th century. From 1956 it was reintroduced.
102600.m: The beaver has returned to Switzerland.

102601.q: At what time of day is the beaver usually active?
102601.e: Beavers are mainly out and about at dusk and at night. That is why you rarely see them, but often see their gnaw marks.
102601.m: The beaver is mainly out and about at night.

102602.q: What does a ranger do in a nature reserve?
102602.e: A ranger makes sure the rules are followed. They also explain nature to visitors.

102603.q: What does a ranger explain to visitors?
a: How to build a mobile phone
102603.e: Rangers explain in a friendly way why you should stay on the path, for example. That way visitors understand how to protect nature.
102603.m: A ranger explains the rules in nature.

102604.q: Which tool does a ranger often use to watch animals from a distance?
102604.e: With binoculars the ranger can see animals from far away. That way they don't disturb them.
102604.m: With binoculars you watch animals without disturbing them.

102605.q: What do rangers sometimes count in their area?
102605.e: Rangers count ibex or birds, for example. That way people know how the animals are doing.
102605.m: Rangers count animals to protect them.

102606.q: Where do rangers work in Switzerland, for example?
102606.e: Park wardens and rangers work in the Swiss National Park. There are also rangers in nature parks and protected areas.
102606.m: Rangers work in parks and protected areas.

102607.q: What does a ranger do if someone leaves rubbish lying around?
102607.e: The ranger politely points out the rules to the person. For serious offences there can also be a fine.
102607.m: Rangers point out the rules in nature.

102608.q: What kind of clothes does a ranger usually wear at work?
102608.e: Rangers are outdoors in all weathers. That is why they need good shoes and weatherproof clothing.
102608.m: Rangers are outdoors in all weathers.

102609.q: Where do children at a forest kindergarten spend the morning?
102609.e: At a forest kindergarten the children are almost always outside in the forest. They play, learn and eat there.
102609.m: At forest kindergarten the children are in the forest.

102610.q: In what weather does the forest kindergarten go outside?
102610.e: Forest kindergarten takes place outside even in rain or cold. Only in storms or thunderstorms do they keep away from the forest for safety.
102610.m: Forest kindergarten is outside in almost any weather.

102611.q: What do children at a forest kindergarten especially need?
102611.e: In the forest it is often wet or cold. Weatherproof clothes and good shoes keep the children warm and dry.
102611.m: In the forest you need weatherproof clothes.

102612.q: In which country was the first forest kindergarten set up?
102612.e: The first forest kindergarten was set up in Denmark in the 1950s. Later there were many forest kindergartens in Switzerland too.
102612.m: The idea of the forest kindergarten comes from Denmark.

102613.q: What do children at a forest kindergarten often play with?
102613.e: The forest has lots to play with: sticks, stones, cones and leaves. The children build dens and figures from them.
102613.m: In the forest, nature is the toy.

102614.q: What must children at a forest kindergarten not simply eat?
102614.e: Some berries and mushrooms in the forest are poisonous. That is why you never eat anything you don't know for sure.
102614.m: Never eat unknown berries and mushrooms.

102615.q: What is often found at the fixed spot of a forest kindergarten?
a: A forest sofa or a tarpaulin
102615.e: Many forest kindergartens have a fixed spot with a wooden seating circle and a tarpaulin against the rain. That is where the children eat their mid-morning snack.
102615.m: At the forest spot there is a seating circle and shelter from the rain.

102616.q: What do children check their bodies for after a day in the forest?
102616.e: Ticks can get onto the skin from grass and bushes. That is why you check your body carefully after being in the forest.
102616.m: After the forest, check your body for ticks.

102617.q: Which animal in the national park whistles loudly when danger threatens?
102617.e: The marmot warns its family with a loud whistle. Then they all quickly flee into their burrow.
102617.m: The marmot warns with a whistle.

102619.q: How long does it take for a plastic bottle to break down in nature?
102619.e: Plastic breaks down very slowly in nature, often only after hundreds of years. In the process, tiny bits of plastic are formed.
102619.m: Plastic stays in nature for a very long time.

102620.q: About how many beavers live in Switzerland today (as of 2022)?
102620.e: A count in 2022 found around 4,900 beavers living in Switzerland. Before 1956 there were none left here.
102620.m: Thousands of beavers live in Switzerland again.

102621.q: Which hare gets a white coat in winter and needs peace in the mountains?
102621.e: The mountain hare lives in the Alps and is white in winter. This keeps it well camouflaged in the snow, but like all wild animals it needs lots of peace.
102621.m: The mountain hare has a white coat in winter.

102622.q: What can you do with flaps or turning boards on some nature trails?
102622.e: Many nature trails have boards that you can flip open or turn. That way you can answer questions and see the answer straight away.
102622.m: On a nature trail you can solve puzzles in a playful way.

102623.q: Which animal is shown in the WWF logo?
102623.e: The WWF logo is a black and white panda. The panda stands for animals that need protecting.
102623.m: The WWF logo is a panda.

102624.q: Why are some plants in Switzerland protected?
102624.e: Some plants are only found in a few places now. They are protected so that they don't disappear.
102624.m: Rare plants are protected so that they don't disappear.

102625.q: Why don't you light a fire directly under trees?
a: It is too wet under trees
The trees take the air away from the fire
102625.e: Sparks and heat rise upwards. That is why branches and leaves above the fire can easily catch fire.
102625.m: Don't light a fire under trees.

102626.q: How can you often tell where the nature trail continues?
102626.e: Nature trails have signposts and often numbered stations. That way you find your way from board to board.
102626.m: Signposts lead from station to station.

102627.q: What does a ranger do if a path is dangerous after a storm?
102627.e: Fallen trees or rockfall can be dangerous. The ranger makes sure that nobody gets hurt.

102628.q: What do some lakes in nature reserves have so you can watch birds without disturbing them?
102628.e: From a bird hide you look out at the water through small windows. The birds can hardly see the people.
102628.m: In a bird hide you see birds without disturbing them.

102629.q: What do children at a forest kindergarten do before their mid-morning snack if there is no tap?
a: Wash their hands with water they brought
Wipe their hands on their trousers
102629.e: There is no tap in the forest. That is why you bring a water container and wash your hands with it.
102629.m: Even in the forest you wash your hands before eating.

102720.q: What are the people who are treated in hospital called?
102720.e: Anyone who is examined and treated in hospital is called a patient. The word comes from Latin and has to do with suffering and patience.
102720.m: Ill people in hospital are called patients.

102721.q: What do you often get around your wrist in hospital so that everyone knows who you are?
102721.e: The patient wristband shows your name and other details. That way the hospital team cannot mix anyone up.
102721.m: The name band on your wrist prevents mix-ups.

102722.q: What do you call the time when you may have visitors in hospital?
102722.e: Many hospitals have fixed visiting hours. That way the patients also have enough time to rest.
102722.m: During visiting hours, family and friends may come.

102723.q: Why should you disinfect your hands at the hospital entrance?
102723.e: Disinfectant kills germs on your hands. That way ill people in hospital are better protected.
102723.m: Clean hands protect ill people from germs.

102724.q: What is the university hospital in Bern called?
102724.e: The large university hospital in Bern is called the Inselspital. Many people simply call it “the Insel”.
102724.m: The Inselspital is the university hospital in Bern.

102725.q: Where do you lie in hospital if you have to stay several days?
102725.e: Anyone who stays overnight in hospital gets a bed in a patient's room. Often you share the room with other patients.
102725.m: In hospital, patients sleep in patients' rooms.

102726.q: Which machine can take a picture of your bones in hospital?
102726.e: X-rays pass through skin but not so easily through bone. That is why you can see the bones on an X-ray picture.
102726.m: An X-ray shows the bones in the body.

102727.q: Why are many doors in hospital especially wide?
102727.e: In hospital, patients are often pushed in their beds from one room to another. That needs wide doors.
102727.m: Wide hospital doors let beds through.

102728.q: What does the doctor use to listen to your heart?
102728.e: A stethoscope has two earpieces and a tube. With it, the doctor listens to your heartbeat and the breathing in your lungs.
102728.m: You listen to the heart and lungs with a stethoscope.

102729.q: What do you call a doctor who especially looks after children?
102729.e: A children's doctor knows about children's illnesses and growth. Many children go for regular check-ups.
102729.m: The children's doctor is there for children.

102730.q: Who looks after teeth that are not healthy?
102730.e: The dentist checks your teeth, finds holes and fills them. You should go for a check-up about once a year.
102730.m: The dentist cares for and repairs teeth.

102731.q: What do you use to measure whether someone has a fever?
102731.e: A thermometer measures body temperature. If it is clearly higher than normal, you have a fever.
102731.m: A thermometer shows whether you have a fever.

102732.q: What does the doctor use to press your tongue down to look into your throat?
102732.e: The flat wooden spatula gently presses the tongue down. That way the doctor can see whether the throat is red or inflamed.
102732.m: The doctor looks into your throat using a wooden spatula.

102733.q: What is the doctor called that a family usually goes to first when someone is ill?
102733.e: The family doctor often knows the family well. If necessary, they send the patient on to a specialist.
102733.m: The family doctor is usually the first place to go.

102734.q: In which room do you wait at the doctor's surgery until it is your turn?
102734.e: At the doctor's surgery, you sit in the waiting room. There are often books and toys there for children.
102734.m: You wait for the doctor in the waiting room.

102735.q: Which card do you show at the doctor's in Switzerland so that the health insurance pays?
102735.e: The insurance card shows which health insurance company you are insured with. Anyone who lives in Switzerland must have health insurance.
102735.m: The insurance card shows your health insurance company.

102736.q: Who often takes temperatures in hospital and helps patients to wash?
102736.e: Nurses look after patients all day long. They measure values, give medicines and help with personal care.
102736.m: Nurses look after patients in hospital.

102737.q: When do nurses work in hospital?
102737.e: Ill people need help at night too. That is why there are nursing staff in hospital around the clock.
102737.m: In hospital, there is care day and night.

102738.q: What do you call work that sometimes happens in the morning, sometimes in the evening and sometimes at night?
102738.e: In shift work, several groups take turns. That way there is always someone at work, even at night.
102738.m: In shift work, people take turns.

102739.q: Which woman is seen as the founder of modern nursing?
102739.e: Florence Nightingale cared for wounded soldiers in the 19th century. She showed how important cleanliness and good care are.

102743.q: What do you use to measure out liquid cough syrup correctly?
102743.e: Syrup often comes with a small measuring cup or measuring spoon. That way you take exactly the right amount.
102743.m: You measure syrup with the measuring cup.

102744.q: Which sign often lights up outside a pharmacy in Switzerland?
102744.e: In Switzerland and many European countries, you can recognise pharmacies by the green cross. It often lights up so that you can see it from far away.
102744.m: A green cross shows a pharmacy.

102745.q: What is the expert called who hands out and explains medicines at the pharmacy?
102745.e: A pharmacist has studied pharmacy. They know exactly how medicines work and how to take them correctly.
102745.m: The pharmacist knows all about medicines.

102746.q: How should medicines be kept at home?
102746.e: Some medicines look like sweets but can be dangerous. That is why they belong up high or in a lockable cupboard.
102746.m: Medicines belong out of children's reach.

102747.q: Where does it say how to take a medicine correctly?
102747.e: Every medicine packet contains a sheet of paper, the package leaflet. It says how much you may take and what to watch out for.
102747.m: The package leaflet explains how to take a medicine.

102748.q: What is a pharmacy called that also helps at night or on Sundays?
102748.e: An emergency pharmacy is available outside normal opening hours too. That way you can get urgently needed medicines even at night.
102748.m: The emergency pharmacy helps at night and on Sundays too.

102749.q: What can you buy at the pharmacy without a prescription?
102749.e: Plasters, creams for insect bites and some simple remedies are available without a prescription. The pharmacist gives you advice.
102749.m: You can get plasters at the pharmacy without a prescription.

102750.q: What does the expiry date on a medicine show?
102750.e: After the expiry date, a medicine may no longer work properly. Out-of-date medicines are taken back to the pharmacy.
102750.m: Out-of-date medicines go back to the pharmacy.

102751.q: Why do children often get an injection at the doctor’s?
102751.e: Many vaccinations are given with an injection. The prick is short and then often protects you for many years.
102751.m: A vaccination is often given as an injection.

102752.q: Where is a vaccination injection usually given?
102752.e: Most vaccines are injected into the muscle of the upper arm. For babies, the thigh is often used.
102752.m: Vaccine injections are usually given in the upper arm.

102753.q: What does the nurse do to the skin before an injection?
102753.e: A swab with disinfectant removes the germs from the skin. That way no germs get into the body with the needle.
102753.m: Before an injection, the skin is disinfected.

102754.q: What is often stuck on the spot after an injection?
102754.e: A small plaster protects the spot until the tiny prick has healed. Often it only bleeds a tiny bit.
102754.m: A plaster goes on the injection spot.

102755.q: What can help if you are scared of an injection?
102755.e: Calm breathing helps you relax. A loose arm hurts less than a tense one.
102755.m: Calm breathing helps against fear of injections.

102756.q: What is at the front of a syringe?
102756.e: At the front of the syringe there is a very thin needle. The medicine flows through it into the body.
102756.m: A syringe has a thin needle at the front.

102757.q: What is taken out of the body with the needle during a blood test?
102757.e: The blood goes into a small tube. It is examined in the laboratory so the doctor can learn more about your health.
102757.m: For a blood test, a little blood is examined.

102758.q: What is the hospital department called that you go to straight away after an accident?
102758.e: In accident and emergency, injured people and people who suddenly become seriously ill are treated at once. Specialists who know all about emergencies work there.
102758.m: Accident and emergency helps immediately after accidents.

102759.q: What do you call a doctor who comes straight to an accident with the ambulance or helicopter?
102759.e: The emergency doctor treats injured people at the scene of the accident. Afterwards they are taken to hospital.
102759.m: The emergency doctor helps right at the scene of the accident.

102760.q: What is the vehicle called that takes sick and injured people quickly to hospital?
102760.e: In Switzerland it is also usually called an ambulance (Ambulanz). It takes sick and injured people to hospital quickly.
102760.m: An ambulance takes people quickly to hospital.

102761.q: Where do very seriously ill people go who have to be watched all the time?
102761.e: In intensive care, the heart, breathing and other values are monitored round the clock. Especially many specialists work there for each patient.
102761.m: In intensive care, seriously ill people are monitored constantly.

102762.q: How does Rega quickly rescue injured people from the mountains?
102762.e: Rega flies helicopters to accidents, including in the mountains. That way injured people get to hospital quickly.
102762.m: Rega flies helicopters to injured people.

102763.q: Who is treated first in accident and emergency?
102763.e: In accident and emergency, staff check how urgently someone needs help. Anyone whose life is in danger goes first, even if others have been waiting longer.
102763.m: In A&E, the most urgent cases go first.

102764.q: What colour are operating clothes often?
102764.e: Green and blue are restful for the eyes when you look at red for a long time. That is why many operating clothes are green or blue.
102764.m: Operating clothes are often green or blue.

102765.q: What is the sport called where you throw a ball into a basket from a wheelchair?
102765.e: In wheelchair basketball the basket is the same height as in normal basketball. It is a sport at the Paralympics.
102765.m: In wheelchair basketball you throw the ball into a basket.

102766.q: What do you call a doctor who carries out operations?
102766.e: Surgeons operate. They treat illnesses and injuries with fine instruments.

102767.q: What is the room called where operations take place?
102767.e: The operating theatre is especially clean and bright. All the equipment needed for an operation is there.
102767.m: Operations take place in the operating theatre.

102768.q: Why does the operating team wear a mask over mouth and nose?
a: So no germs get into the wound
102768.e: When you speak and breathe, tiny droplets come out of your mouth. The mask holds them back so the open wound stays clean.
102768.m: The mask in the operating theatre keeps germs away from the wound.

102769.q: What does the operating team wear on their hands?
102769.e: The gloves are sterile and only used once. Jewellery is taken off before an operation.
102769.m: During an operation you wear sterile gloves.

102770.q: What does the surgeon do with the cut in the skin at the end of an operation?
102770.e: The wound is closed with stitches, clips or glue. That way it can heal well.
102770.m: After the operation, the wound is closed.

102771.q: Where in the tummy does it often hurt with appendicitis?
a: Right at the top under the ribs
102771.e: The appendix is in the bottom right of the tummy. If it is inflamed, it often hurts there and you need an operation.
102771.m: An inflamed appendix hurts in the bottom right of the tummy.

102772.q: What does “sterile” mean for instruments used in an operation?
102772.e: Sterile instruments are made germ-free with great heat or in other ways. That way no germs get into the wound during the operation.

102773.q: What is the small, very sharp knife used for operating called?
102773.e: With the scalpel the surgeon makes fine, precise cuts. It is sharper than any kitchen knife.
102773.m: The knife for operating is called a scalpel.

102774.q: What happens under a general anaesthetic?
a: You sleep deeply and feel nothing
102774.e: Under a general anaesthetic you sleep very deeply. So you feel no pain from the operation and notice nothing.
102774.m: Under a general anaesthetic you sleep and feel no pain.

102775.q: Who makes sure during an operation that you sleep deeply and feel nothing?
102775.e: The anaesthetist gives the anaesthetic. She stays close by during the whole operation and looks after you.
102775.m: The anaesthetist looks after you during the operation.

102776.q: What are you not allowed to do for a few hours before an anaesthetic?
102776.e: Before an anaesthetic your stomach must be empty, so you must not have eaten. That way no food can get from the stomach into the lungs during the anaesthetic.
102776.m: Before an anaesthetic your stomach must be empty.

102777.q: What is it called when only a small area is made pain-free, for example at the dentist?
102777.e: With a local anaesthetic only one area becomes numb. You stay awake but feel no pain there.
102777.m: With a local anaesthetic you stay awake.

102778.q: In which room do you wake up after an operation with an anaesthetic?
102778.e: In the recovery room you are watched closely until you are fully awake again. Then you go to your ward room.
102778.m: After the anaesthetic you wake up in the recovery room.

102779.q: How do children often receive the anaesthetic?
102779.e: Children often breathe in the anaesthetic through a mask. Sometimes they get it through a thin tube into a vein.
102779.m: Children often breathe in the anaesthetic through a mask.

102780.q: What does the anaesthetist monitor during an operation?
102780.e: Machines constantly show how the heart is beating and how well you are breathing. That way anyone notices at once if something is wrong.
102780.m: During the anaesthetic, heart and breathing are monitored.

102781.q: How do you often feel right after waking up from an anaesthetic?
102781.e: The anaesthetic needs some time to leave the body. That is why you are often still tired and a little confused afterwards.
102781.m: After an anaesthetic you are often still tired.

102782.q: What is a hospital called that only treats children and teenagers?
102782.e: In a children’s hospital everything is set up for children. The doctors and nurses are also specialised in children.
102782.m: Children are treated in a children’s hospital.

102783.q: What do many people call the Children’s Hospital Zurich for short?
102783.e: The University Children’s Hospital Zurich is often simply called “Kispi”. It is one of the largest children’s hospitals in Switzerland.
102783.m: The Children’s Hospital Zurich is called Kispi for short.

102784.q: Who cares for the sick children in a children’s hospital?
102784.e: In the children’s hospital, nurses look after the sick children day and night. They work closely with the doctors.
102784.m: In the children’s hospital, nurses care for the children.

102785.q: What do large children’s hospitals have for children who must stay a long time?
102785.e: In the hospital school children keep learning so they don’t miss too much at school. The lessons are adapted to their illness.
102785.m: In the hospital school, sick children keep learning.

102786.q: Can parents stay with their child in a children’s hospital?
102786.e: For sick children it is important that mum or dad is there. That is why parents can often even sleep in the room.
102786.m: Parents can often stay with their sick child.

102787.q: What do you call a doctor who especially treats children?
102787.e: A paediatrician knows all about illnesses in babies and children. The technical word for children’s medicine is paediatrics.

102788.q: What do many children’s wards have so children can take their mind off things?
102788.e: In the playroom there are games, books and craft things. There children can forget for a while that they are ill.
102788.m: In the playroom, sick children can play.

102789.q: What can children often bring to hospital to feel more comfortable?
102789.e: A familiar cuddly toy gives comfort and security. Pets are usually not allowed in hospital for reasons of hygiene.
102789.m: A cuddly toy helps against homesickness in hospital.

102790.q: How many large drive wheels does a normal wheelchair have?
102790.e: A normal wheelchair has two large wheels at the back to push it along. At the front it has two small wheels for steering.
102790.m: A wheelchair has two large drive wheels.

102791.q: What helps people in a wheelchair get over a step?
102791.e: A ramp is a sloping surface instead of a step. You can roll up and down it in a wheelchair.
102791.m: A ramp makes steps passable for wheelchairs.

102792.q: How do you move a wheelchair without a motor forwards?
a: With your hands on the large wheels
With a crank on the seat
102792.e: A ring, the push rim, is fixed to the large wheel. You hold it with your hands and push the wheelchair forwards.
102792.m: You drive a wheelchair with your hands on the large wheels.

102793.q: What is the name of the famous Swiss wheelchair athlete nicknamed “Silver Bullet”?
102793.e: Marcel Hug is a wheelchair athlete from Thurgau. He has already won several gold medals at the Paralympic Games.
102793.m: Marcel Hug is a successful Swiss wheelchair athlete.

102794.q: What are the big sports games for athletes with disabilities called?
102794.e: Like the Olympic Games, the Paralympics take place every four years. There are wheelchair races there, for example.
102794.m: People with disabilities compete at the Paralympics.

102795.q: In which village in the canton of Lucerne is the Swiss Paraplegic Centre?
102795.e: The Swiss Paraplegic Centre in Nottwil treats people with paraplegia. Many learn there how to manage their everyday life in a wheelchair.
102795.m: The Paraplegic Centre is in Nottwil.

102796.e: An electric wheelchair has an electric motor and a battery. It is usually steered with a small joystick.
102796.m: An electric wheelchair runs on a motor and a battery.

102797.q: What background colour does the wheelchair sign on parking spaces usually have?
102797.e: The international sign shows a white wheelchair on a blue background. It marks parking spaces, toilets and entrances for wheelchair users.
102797.m: The wheelchair sign is white on a blue background.

102798.q: When do you often need crutches?
102798.e: With crutches you put less weight on the injured leg. That helps it heal better.
102798.m: Crutches take the weight off an injured leg.

102799.q: How many crutches do people usually use?
102799.e: Usually you walk with two crutches, one in each hand. That is safer and spreads your weight well.
102799.m: Usually you walk with two crutches.

102800.q: Where do you support yourself with forearm crutches?
102800.e: You hold the grip with your hand and your forearm rests in a cuff. That is where the name forearm crutch comes from.
102800.m: With forearm crutches you lean on your hands and forearms.

102801.q: What do you often get around your leg when a bone is broken?
102801.e: The cast goes hard and keeps the broken bone still. That way it can grow back together in the right position.
102801.m: A cast keeps a broken bone still.

102802.q: What does a crutch have at the bottom so it doesn’t slip?
102802.e: The rubber tip at the bottom grips the floor well. When it is worn out, it should be replaced.
102802.m: The rubber tip stops the crutch slipping.

102803.q: When climbing stairs on crutches, which leg goes onto the step first?
102803.e: Going up, the healthy leg leads because it has to lift the body. The crutches and the injured leg follow.
102803.m: Going upstairs, the healthy leg goes first.

102804.q: How do you adjust crutches to a person’s height?
102804.e: Crutches have holes and a button that let you set the length. The grips should be roughly at wrist height.
102804.m: Crutches can be adjusted in length.

102805.q: Who often shows you how to walk properly with crutches?
102805.e: The physiotherapist helps people move well again after injuries. She also practises walking with crutches.
102805.m: The physiotherapist practises walking with crutches.

102806.q: What does a hospital bed have underneath so it can be pushed?
102806.e: Hospital beds have wheels underneath. That way patients can be wheeled in their bed to examinations.
102806.m: Hospital beds have wheels for pushing.

102807.q: What can you adjust with buttons on a hospital bed?
102807.e: A motor raises and lowers the bed. The head end can also be raised so you can sit comfortably.
102807.m: On a hospital bed, height and backrest can be adjusted.

102808.q: What do you press in a hospital bed when you need help from the nurses?
102808.e: There is a call button by the bed. When you press it, the nurses know you need help.
102808.m: You call the nurses with the call button.

102809.q: Why does a hospital bed often have rails at the side?
102809.e: The side rails protect you from falling out of bed. That is important after an anaesthetic or at night, for example.
102809.m: Side rails stop you falling out.

102810.q: What stands next to the hospital bed for your drinking bottle, book and glasses?
102810.e: On the bedside table you have the most important things within reach. Often you can fold out a tray and eat at it.
102810.m: Things within reach go on the bedside table.

102811.q: Why can a hospital bed be raised?
a: So the nurses can work without hurting their backs
So you can look out of the window
102811.e: At the right height the nurse doesn’t have to bend down so far. That protects her back.
102811.m: A raised bed protects the nurses’ backs.

102812.q: What often hangs on a stand next to the bed and puts fluid into a vein?
102812.e: With a drip, fluid drips slowly through a thin tube into a vein. That way you get water or medicine.
102812.m: A drip slowly puts fluid into a vein.

102813.q: Why do the wheels of a hospital bed have brakes?
a: So the bed doesn’t roll away
102813.e: When the bed is standing in the room, the wheels are locked. That way it doesn’t roll away when someone gets in or out.
102813.m: Locked wheels hold the hospital bed in place.

102814.q: What is special about a university hospital?
a: It is only open at night
102814.e: At a university hospital, medical students learn from experienced doctors. A lot of research is also done there.
102814.m: Doctors are trained at a university hospital.

102815.q: What does the nurse bring to the patients’ beds at set times?
102815.e: The nurses make sure everyone gets the right medicine at the right time. This is set out exactly in the doctor’s plan.
102815.m: The nurses bring the medicines at the right time.

102816.q: What helps wheelchair users in a building with several floors?
102816.e: With a lift you can reach every floor without stairs. That is why public buildings need lifts.
102816.m: A lift takes a wheelchair to every floor.

102817.q: On what are injured people pushed lying down into the ambulance?
102817.e: The stretcher often has wheels and straps. That way injured people can be carried safely lying down.
102817.m: Injured people are carried lying down on a stretcher.

a: A test to find something out
102818.e: In an experiment you try something out on purpose. That is how you find out how nature works.
102818.m: With an experiment you find something out.

102819.q: Who does lots of experiments as their job?
102819.e: Scientists ask questions and test them with experiments. That is how new knowledge is created.

102820.q: What do you put on to protect your eyes during experiments with liquids?
102820.e: Safety goggles protect your eyes from splashes. They fit closely and are made of strong plastic.
102820.m: In experiments, safety goggles protect your eyes.

102821.q: Why do you often do an experiment several times?
a: To check whether it always turns out the same
Because it isn't allowed the first time
So that you have more tidying up to do
102821.e: If an experiment turns out the same several times, you can trust the result more. A single time could also be chance.
102821.m: Repeating an experiment makes the result more certain.

102822.q: What is the text called in which you write down how an experiment went?
102822.e: The report lists the materials, the steps and the result. That way someone else can repeat the experiment exactly.
102822.m: In a report you write an experiment down exactly.

102823.q: Who must always be there during experiments with fire?
102823.e: Fire can quickly become dangerous. That is why such experiments are only done when an adult is watching.
102823.m: An adult is always there for experiments with fire.

102824.q: What is the room called where scientists do experiments?
102824.e: A laboratory is set up for experiments. It has measuring instruments, sinks and safety equipment.
102824.m: Scientists do their experiments in a laboratory.

102825.q: In which town is the Technorama, where you can try out lots of experiments yourself?
102825.e: The Swiss Science Center Technorama is in Winterthur in the canton of Zurich. It has hundreds of hands-on experiments.
102825.m: At the Technorama in Winterthur you can experiment yourself.

102826.q: What do you do after an experiment?
a: Tidy up and wash your hands
102826.e: After the experiment the materials are put away and the place is cleaned. Washing your hands is important, especially after handling substances.
102826.m: After an experiment you tidy up and wash your hands.

102827.q: You want to test whether a plant grows better with more water. What should be different between the two plants?
102827.e: If you only change the water, you know exactly where the difference comes from. Everything else stays the same.
102827.m: In a fair test you change only one thing.

102828.q: What do you call it when you say before the experiment what will probably happen?
102828.e: Before the experiment you think about what could happen. This idea is called a prediction.
102828.m: A prediction says what will probably happen.

102829.q: What is the scientific word for a guess you want to test?
102829.e: In science a guess like this is called a hypothesis. With an experiment you check whether it is right.
102829.m: A hypothesis is a scientific guess.

102830.q: Is a prediction allowed to be wrong?
102830.e: A prediction is an idea, not a certain answer. You learn a lot from a wrong prediction too.
102830.m: Even a wrong prediction helps you learn.

102831.q: When do you make a prediction?
102831.e: The prediction comes first. Then the experiment shows whether it is right.
102831.m: You make a prediction before the experiment.

102832.q: Which sentence beginning suits a prediction well?
102832.e: With “I think that ...” you say what you expect. You are not yet sure.
102832.m: A prediction often begins with “I think that”.

102833.q: You predict that a stone will sink in water. How do you check that?
a: I put it in the sun
102833.e: You check a prediction with a suitable experiment. Here you simply put the stone in water and watch.
102833.m: You check a prediction with a suitable test.

102834.q: What do you do if the experiment doesn't confirm your prediction?
a: You think of a new prediction
102834.e: An honest result is more important than a correct prediction. You think again and test again.
102834.m: If the result doesn't fit, you make a new prediction.

102835.q: What do you base a good prediction on?
a: On a roll of the dice
On the colour of your clothes
On the day of the week
102835.e: A good prediction is not just a guess. You think about earlier experiences and what you have already learnt.
102835.m: A good prediction is built on knowledge.

102836.e: An observation describes what really happens. Words like “maybe” or “I think” belong to a prediction.
102836.m: An observation describes what really happens.

102838.q: What helps you record an observation accurately?
102838.e: With a drawing or a photo you can still see exactly later what it looked like. You also write a few sentences.

102839.q: In an experiment, what do you use to measure how long something takes?
102839.e: A stopwatch measures time exactly. You start it at the beginning and stop it at the end.
102839.m: A stopwatch measures how long something takes.

102840.q: How many degrees does the thermometer show when water freezes into ice?
102840.e: At 0 degrees Celsius water freezes into ice. At 100 degrees it boils.

102841.q: Why must you not put anything in your mouth during experiments?
102841.e: In experiments you often don't know whether a substance is safe. That is why nothing is tasted.

102842.q: What is especially important for a good observation?
102842.e: A good observation describes exactly what happened. You also write down what you didn't expect.
102842.m: A good observation is accurate and honest.

102843.q: In an experiment, what do you use to measure how long something is?
102843.e: A tape measure and a ruler show length in centimetres and metres. That way you can measure, for example, how far something flew.
102843.m: You measure lengths with a tape measure.

102844.q: What happens if you lay a flat sheet of paper as a bridge between two cups and put a coin on it?
102844.e: A flat sheet of paper bends very easily. Even one coin pushes it down.
102844.m: A flat sheet holds almost nothing.

102845.q: How do you fold the paper so that the bridge holds much more?
102845.e: Folded in a zigzag, the paper becomes much stiffer. Then the bridge holds lots of coins.
102845.m: Paper folded in a zigzag holds much more.

102846.q: Why does folded paper hold more than flat paper?
102846.e: Because of the folds, the paper can no longer bend so easily. The material is the same, only the shape is different.

102847.q: Which shape inside makes cardboard for parcels especially strong?
102847.e: Corrugated cardboard has a wavy layer of paper inside. This shape makes the cardboard strong but still light.
102847.m: Waves inside cardboard make it strong.

102848.q: What happens if you roll a sheet of paper into a tube and stand it up?
102848.e: A tube is a very strong shape. You can even put a book on it.
102848.m: A paper tube is surprisingly strong.

102849.q: What makes good weights to put on a paper bridge to test it?
102849.e: Coins are small, all weigh the same and are easy to count. That way you can compare which bridge holds the most.
102849.m: You can test paper bridges with coins.

102850.q: Which shape do many old stone bridges have, because it holds weight well?
102850.e: An arch passes the weight sideways down into the piers. That is why some arch bridges have stood for hundreds of years.
102850.m: An arch makes a bridge strong.

102851.q: What is the famous wooden bridge in Lucerne called?
102851.e: The Chapel Bridge crosses the River Reuss in Lucerne. It is said to be one of the oldest covered wooden bridges in Europe.
102851.m: The Chapel Bridge is the landmark of Lucerne.

102852.e: The air in the balloon is squeezed together. When it rushes out at the back, the balloon is pushed forwards.
102852.m: Air rushing out drives the balloon rocket.

102853.q: The air rushes out of the back of the balloon. Which way does the balloon move?
102853.e: The air is pushed backwards and pushes the balloon forwards. Balloon and air move in opposite directions.
102853.m: The balloon flies the opposite way to the air rushing out.

102854.q: If you let go of a blown-up balloon, the air shoots out of the back and the balloon zooms forwards. What is this called?
102854.e: When something is pushed away backwards, the rest moves forwards. This is called recoil.

102855.q: For a balloon rocket, what do you thread onto a tight string?
102855.e: The balloon is taped to a drinking straw. The straw slides easily along the string.
102855.m: The drinking straw slides along the string.

102856.q: What is the tight string for in a balloon rocket?
102856.e: Without a string, the balloon would fly around wildly. With the string, it flies straight.
102856.m: The string guides the balloon rocket straight ahead.

102857.q: What usually happens if you blow the balloon up more?
102857.e: More air in the balloon can rush out for longer and more strongly. That is why it usually flies further.
102857.m: More air makes the balloon rocket fly further.

102858.q: If you let go of a blown-up balloon, it zooms off because the air rushes out of the back. What flies in the same way?
102858.e: A space rocket also pushes gases out of the back. That makes it fly in the other direction, even in space.
102858.m: Space rockets fly like a balloon that has been let go.

102859.q: Which scientist explained that every force has an equal opposite force?
102859.e: Isaac Newton described the laws of motion over 300 years ago. One of them says that for every force there is an opposite force.
102859.m: Isaac Newton explained action and reaction.

102860.q: Which container is good for a home-made lava lamp?
102860.e: In a see-through bottle or glass you can see the colourful bubbles rising. In a tin or a pot you would see none of it.
102860.m: For a lava lamp you need a see-through container.

102861.q: Why does oil float on water?
a: Oil is lighter than the same amount of water
Oil is more colourful than water
102861.e: A litre of oil weighs less than a litre of water. Anything lighter than the same amount of water floats on top.
102861.m: Oil is lighter than the same amount of water.

102862.q: What do you use to colour the water in the lava lamp?
102862.e: A few drops of food colouring make the water nice and colourful. That way you can see the movements better.
102862.m: Food colouring makes the water colourful.

102863.q: Which liquid in the lava lamp does the food colouring mix with?
102863.e: Food colouring dissolves in water. That is why it only colours the water, and the oil stays clear.
102863.m: The colouring only mixes with the water.

102864.q: What do you put into the lava lamp to make bubbles rise?
102864.e: The fizzy tablet bubbles in the water and makes gas bubbles. The bubbles carry coloured water up with them.
102864.m: A fizzy tablet makes the lava lamp bubble.

102865.q: Why do the coloured drops sink back down from the top?
a: Because the gas escapes at the top
102865.e: At the top the gas bubbles burst and the gas escapes. Without a bubble, the water drop is heavier than the oil again and sinks.
102865.m: Without a gas bubble, the water drop sinks again.

102866.q: What happens if you shake oil and water hard and then wait?
102866.e: Shaking makes tiny droplets of oil. But after a while the oil gathers at the top again.
102866.m: Oil and water always separate again.

102867.q: What happens once the fizzy tablet has completely dissolved?
102867.e: The bubbles only form while the tablet is fizzing. With a new tablet it starts again.
102867.m: Without a tablet there are no new bubbles.

102868.q: What holds the card on the full, upside-down glass of water?
102868.e: The air around us presses on everything, including the card. This pressure is strong enough to hold the water in the glass.
102868.m: Air pressure holds the card on the glass.

102869.q: With the upside-down glass, from which direction does the air press against the card?
102869.e: The air around us presses in all directions, including from below. That is why the card doesn't fall off.

102870.q: How full is it best to fill the glass for the card experiment?
102870.e: If the glass is full to the brim, there is hardly any air inside pressing against the card. That way the experiment works best.
102870.m: For the card experiment you fill the glass right up.

102871.q: Where is the best place to do the experiment with the upside-down glass?
102871.e: If the card does slip, the water simply runs into the sink. That way nothing gets wet or damaged.
102871.m: You do water experiments over the sink.

102872.q: What happens if you hold the glass with the card at an angle and air gets in?
102872.e: If air gets into the glass, it presses from inside too. Then the air pressure from below no longer holds the card.
102872.m: If air gets into the glass, the card falls off.

102873.q: What makes a good card for the upside-down glass of water?
102873.e: The card must be smooth and tight and must not let water through. A postcard or a beer mat works well.
102873.m: A smooth postcard works well for the experiment.

102875.q: What happens to the balloon rocket when there is no more air in the balloon?
102875.e: Without air rushing out, there is nothing driving it any more. The balloon rocket slows down and stops on the string.
102875.m: Without air, the balloon rocket has nothing to drive it.

102876.q: What forms when you drip lots of drops of water onto a coin?
102876.e: The water doesn't run off straight away but bulges up over the coin. It looks like a little dome.
102876.m: A hill of water bulges up on the coin.

102877.q: Which animal can walk on water without sinking?
102877.e: The pond skater is a light insect. The surface of the water acts like a thin skin and holds it up.
102877.m: The skin on the water holds up the pond skater.

102878.q: What can you use to drip water onto a coin very precisely, drop by drop?
102878.e: With a pipette you can release single drops precisely. That way you can count them easily too.
102878.m: You drip precisely with a pipette.

102879.q: What happens when there are too many drops on the coin?
102879.e: At some point the hill of water is too heavy. Then the skin of the water breaks and the water flows over the edge.
102879.m: If the hill of water gets too big, it spills over.

102880.q: Which Swiss coin will probably hold the most drops of water?
102880.e: The 5-franc coin is the biggest Swiss coin. Its large surface has room for the most water.
102880.m: A big coin holds more drops.

102881.q: What do you write down as the result of the coin experiment?
102881.e: You count the drops until the water spills over. That way you can compare different coins.
102881.m: In the coin experiment you count the drops.

102882.q: What do you do with the coin before the coin experiment?
a: You make it clean and dry
You put it in the freezer
102882.e: Dirt and grease on the coin change the result. With a clean, dry coin the comparison is fair.
102882.m: For the coin experiment you need a clean coin.

102883.q: Why do you drip slowly and carefully in the coin experiment?
a: So the skin of the water doesn't break
102883.e: A fast or hard drop can destroy the domed skin of the water. Then the water spills over too early.
102883.m: Dripping carefully protects the skin of the water.

102884.q: What happens to the bottle diver when you squeeze the bottle?
102884.e: Squeezing presses water into the diver. It gets heavier and sinks to the bottom.
102884.m: When you squeeze the bottle, the diver sinks.

102885.q: What happens when you let go of the bottle again?
a: The diver stays at the bottom
102885.e: When you let go, the air in the diver pushes the water out again. It gets lighter and rises.
102885.m: When you let go, the diver rises again.

102886.q: What is inside the bottle diver so that it floats at the top?
102886.e: The air bubble in the diver makes it light. That is why it floats at the top as long as nobody squeezes.
102886.m: The air bubble makes the diver float.

102887.q: What happens to the air bubble in the diver when you squeeze the bottle?
102887.e: Air can be squeezed together, but water hardly at all. That is why the air bubble gets smaller when you squeeze.

102888.q: What can you make a simple bottle diver from?
102888.e: A plastic pipette with a little air in it works well. Weighed down with a bit of modelling clay, it only just floats.
102888.m: A pipette can become a bottle diver.

102889.q: What is the bottle filled with for the bottle diver?
102889.e: The bottle is filled to the top with water and closed tightly. There is only air in the diver itself.
102889.m: The bottle for the bottle diver is full of water.

102890.q: Which scientist is the bottle diver, also called the “Cartesian diver”, named after?
102890.e: The name recalls the French scholar René Descartes. In Latin he was called Cartesius.
102890.m: The Cartesian diver is named after René Descartes.

102891.q: Which animal has a swim bladder to rise or sink in the water?
102891.e: The swim bladder is like a little balloon in the fish's belly. With more air in it the fish rises, with less air it sinks.
102891.m: Fish use their swim bladder to float at the right depth.

102892.q: What is a water rocket usually made from?
102892.e: A plastic bottle is light and can take a lot of pressure. That is why it works well as the body of the rocket.
102892.m: A water rocket is made from a plastic bottle.

102893.q: Which way does the water spray when the water rocket takes off?
102893.e: The pressure in the bottle forces the water out hard at the bottom. That makes the rocket shoot upwards.
102893.m: The water sprays down and the rocket flies up.

102894.q: What builds up in the water rocket when you pump?
102894.e: More and more air is pressed into the bottle. At some point the pressure is so great that the stopper gives way.
102894.m: High pressure builds up in the water rocket.

102895.q: Roughly how much water do you put into a water rocket?
102895.e: You need water to push out and room for the pumped air. About a third water often works well.
102895.m: You fill a water rocket about a third full.

102896.q: What do you stick onto a water rocket so that it flies straight?
102896.e: The fins at the bottom make the rocket fly steadily. Without them it would easily wobble.
102896.m: Fins make the water rocket fly straight.

102897.q: Where do you launch a water rocket?
102897.e: A water rocket flies high and sprays lots of water. That is why it needs plenty of space outdoors.
102897.m: Water rockets are launched outside in a field.

102898.q: Why do you keep your distance when a water rocket is launched?
a: It takes off suddenly and fast
102898.e: The rocket shoots off with great force. Anyone standing too close can be hit or sprayed with water.
102898.m: Keep your distance when a water rocket is launched.

102899.q: Why can a steel sewing needle lie on top of water?
a: The water's surface holds it up like a skin
102899.e: The water particles at the surface hold together. This makes a thin layer that can hold up a light needle.
102899.m: The surface of water can hold up a light needle.

102900.q: What do you put the needle on to place it carefully on the water?
102900.e: The paper lays the needle very gently on the water. That way the water's surface isn't broken.
102900.m: Kitchen roll lets you lay the needle gently on the water.

102901.q: What happens to the kitchen roll under the needle after a short time?
a: It soaks up water and sinks
102901.e: The paper soaks up water and gets heavy. It sinks, but the needle stays on top.
102901.m: The wet paper sinks and the needle stays on top.

102902.q: What happens if you put a drop of washing-up liquid next to the floating needle?
102902.e: Washing-up liquid weakens the skin on the water. Then it can no longer hold up the needle.
102902.m: Washing-up liquid makes the floating needle sink.

102903.q: What happens if you put the needle into the water point first?
102903.e: The point pierces the surface of the water. Then the water can no longer hold up the needle.

102904.q: Which insect walks on the surface of ponds?
102904.e: The pond skater is light and has long, water-repellent legs. That way it can walk across the water without sinking.
102904.m: The pond skater can walk across water.

102905.q: What can you make from a magnetised needle floating on water?
102905.e: A magnetised needle on water turns to point north and south. Like a compass, it shows the direction.
102905.m: A floating magnetised needle points north.

102906.q: What does a steel nail do when you throw it into water?
102906.e: Steel is much heavier than the same amount of water. That is why a nail sinks.
102906.m: Steel is much heavier than the same amount of water.

102907.q: What can you see in the water around the floating needle?
102907.e: The needle pushes the surface of the water down a little. The water's skin bends but doesn't break.
102907.m: The needle makes a small dent in the water.

102908.q: What rises from a candle that has just gone out?
102908.e: The wick is still hot and gives off smoke. You can see a thin grey thread rising.
102908.m: A candle that has gone out still smokes for a short time.

102909.q: Which part of the air does a flame need to burn?
102909.e: As it burns, a flame uses up oxygen from the air. Without enough oxygen it goes out.

102910.q: When does a candle under a big glass go out, compared with a small glass?
102910.e: More air is trapped in the big glass. That is why the candle can burn for longer there.
102910.m: Under a big glass the candle burns for longer.

102911.q: Which gas makes the fizzy bubbles in sparkling mineral water?
102911.e: Carbon dioxide is dissolved in sparkling mineral water. When you open the bottle, it rises as bubbles.
102911.m: The bubbles in sparkling water are carbon dioxide.

102912.q: Why does a lid help if oil is burning in the pan?
a: It takes the air away from the fire
102912.e: Just like with the glass over the candle, no fresh air can reach the flame under the lid. The fire is smothered.
102912.m: A lid smothers a fire in the pan.

102913.q: Which blanket can you use to smother small fires?
102913.e: A fire blanket is made of material that doesn't burn. You put it over the fire and so take away its air.
102913.m: A fire blanket smothers small fires.

102914.q: Besides fuel and air, what does a fire need?
102914.e: A fire needs fuel, air and heat. If one of them is missing, the fire goes out.
102914.m: Fire needs fuel, air and heat.

102915.q: What is the main part of a magnifying glass?
102915.e: The most important part of a magnifying glass is the lens. It is thicker in the middle than at the edge.
102915.m: A magnifying glass has a lens that is thicker in the middle.

102916.q: Why must you never look at the sun through a magnifying glass?
a: Otherwise the magnifying glass goes blind
The magnifying glass melts straight away
102916.e: A magnifying glass focuses sunlight. The bright, focused light can badly injure your eyes.
102916.m: Never look at the sun through a magnifying glass.

102917.q: Why shouldn't a magnifying glass lie in bright sunshine on dry leaves?
102917.e: The magnifying glass focuses sunlight onto a small, hot spot. Dry leaves or paper can catch fire there.
102917.m: A magnifying glass in the sun can start a fire.

102918.q: What can you easily discover on a leaf with a magnifying glass?
102918.e: With a magnifying glass you can see the fine veins in a leaf. Water flows through them in the leaf.
102918.m: With a magnifying glass you can see the fine veins of a leaf.

102919.q: How do you hold a magnifying glass to see something sharply?
a: You slowly move it closer or further away
You shake it quickly back and forth
You hold it behind your head
102919.e: With every magnifying glass there is a distance at which the image is sharp. You find it by slowly moving the glass.
102919.m: Move the magnifying glass slowly until the image is sharp.

102920.q: How many legs do you see on a beetle with a magnifying glass?
102920.e: Beetles are insects. All insects have six legs.
102920.m: Insects such as beetles have six legs.

a: A pot with a magnifying glass in the lid
A cup for drinking in the forest
102921.e: A bug viewer is a see-through pot. There is a magnifying glass in the lid, so you can look at small animals magnified.
102921.m: A bug viewer is a pot with a magnifying glass in the lid.

102922.q: What do you do with an animal after looking at it in a bug viewer?
a: You let it go where you found it
You leave it in the pot
You give it to your neighbour
102922.e: Small animals belong in their habitat. That is why you let them go again where you found them after a short time.
102922.m: After watching animals, let them go where you found them.

102923.q: What is the longest a small animal should stay in a bug viewer?
102923.e: In the pot the animal is stressed and can dry out or get too hot. That is why you only watch it briefly.
102923.m: An animal only stays in the bug viewer briefly.

102924.q: Where should a bug viewer with an animal inside not be placed?
102924.e: In the sun it quickly gets very hot inside the pot. That can harm the animal.
102924.m: Never put a bug viewer with an animal in bright sunshine.

102925.q: How many legs do you count on a spider in a bug viewer?
102925.e: Spiders have eight legs. That is why they are not insects, because insects have six legs.

102926.q: What is the best way to get a beetle into a bug viewer?
a: Gently push it in with a leaf
Grab it tightly with your fingers
Catch it with a net made of water
102926.e: Small animals are delicate. Use a leaf or a brush to push them carefully into the pot.
102926.m: Gently push small animals into the bug viewer with a leaf.

102927.q: Which animal fits well into a bug viewer?
102927.e: A bug viewer is small. It is suitable for very small animals such as ladybirds, ants or woodlice.
102927.m: Only very small animals fit into a bug viewer.

102928.q: What can you see well on a woodlouse in a bug viewer?
102928.e: Woodlice have lots of little legs, usually fourteen. They don't have wings, fur or feathers.
102928.m: Woodlice have lots of little legs.

102929.q: What do you need binoculars for?
a: To see faraway things up close
To look at small things in a pot
To make light in the dark
102929.e: Binoculars bring faraway things closer. That way you can see a bird on a distant tree clearly, for example.
102929.m: With binoculars you see faraway things up close.

102930.q: How many tubes do binoculars usually have?
102930.e: Binoculars have two tubes, one for each eye. That way you look with both eyes at the same time.
102930.m: Binoculars have two tubes, one for each eye.

102931.q: What does the number 8 mean on binoculars marked “8x42”?
102931.e: The first number tells you how strongly the binoculars magnify. With 8, a bird looks eight times closer.
102931.m: The first number on binoculars shows how strongly they magnify.

102932.q: Where must you never look with binoculars?
102932.e: Binoculars focus light. Looking at the sun can damage your eyes for ever.
102932.m: Never look at the sun with binoculars.

102933.e: Most binoculars have a focus wheel in the middle. You use it to make the image sharp.
102933.m: You focus binoculars with the focus wheel.

102934.q: Why are binoculars good for watching birds?
a: You don't have to get close
You can catch the birds with them
102934.e: With binoculars you stay far away. That way you don't disturb the birds and they don't fly off.
102934.m: With binoculars you watch animals without disturbing them.

102935.q: What is the strap on binoculars for?
a: You hang them round your neck
You tie flowers together with it
You pull fish out with it
102935.e: You put the strap round your neck. That way the binoculars don't fall and your hands are free.
102935.m: You carry binoculars on a strap round your neck.
